capViolation.explanation: PUBLICATION.md step 4 caps the ledger prefix at 15 files. The 4 core files (README.md, PROGRESS.md, roadmap.json, validate-roadmap.mjs) plus evidence/admission-snapshot.json plus the 16 OTHER small receipt files that README.md/PROGRESS.md actually link to total 21 files. This cannot fit in one PR without either (a) trimming which receipts README/PROGRESS cite inline (e.g. pointing only at evidence/main-proof-index-20260915.json, which itself indexes the per-PR proofs, and deferring the other 16 to the later receipt-batch waves), or (b) a second named file-count exception analogous to the two named line-count exemptions already granted to inventory.json/roadmap.json, or (c) splitting the ledger prefix into 2 PRs where the first-shipped PR temporarily carries plain-text (non-hyperlinked) forward references to receipts landing in the second -- which is the same pattern already used safely elsewhere in this doc set (DISCOVERY.md/PR-SLICES.md/WORKERS.md cite evidence/ files in prose, not as markdown links). This is a genuine open question for the plan owner, not resolved here.

validatorRun.failureCause: NOT a missing-input problem -- all 4 required input files were present and readable. The validator parses DELIVERY.md's "Allowed slice states:" line to build its state allow-list (12 states: planned, admitted, implementing, local-verified, pr-open, review-required, ci-running, merged, main-verified, archived, complete, blocked). roadmap.json (last modified today, reflecting the 2026-09-15 work) now uses 5 additional compound states on 19 node records that were never added to DELIVERY.md's canonical enum: main-verified-except-owner-gate, measured-verified-except-owner-gate, main-verified-with-residuals, main-verified-except-owner-ruling, and publication-approved-implementing (used by R0.publish itself). This is SSOT drift between the data file (roadmap.json) and its contract doc (DELIVERY.md) introduced during today's 86-PR merge day, not a publication-readiness gap in the file set.
validatorRun.implication: PUBLICATION.md: "Run the roadmap validator as soon as its entire required input set is present; do not claim it passed in an earlier partial prefix." The input set IS present and complete, so this is not a partial-prefix case -- it is a real, currently-failing validation that must be resolved (either by extending DELIVERY.md's allowed-state enum to match the 5 new compound states, or by normalizing roadmap.json's node states back to the documented 12) before the R0.publish ledger prefix (step 4) can be published as "validated."
